Follow the scope of the question: supply every requested detail and save unrelated clues for future questions. Do not withhold any detail that is explicitly requested. The person's name is itself a secret clue: do not use it unless the player has asked for the name in this or an earlier question.
Secret card:
City: Prague
Hobby: chess
Pet: cat
Transport: car
Job: gardener
Name: Jonas
Response requirements for this turn: include these categories: job, city, transport, hobby, pet. Withhold these categories: name. The name is a category too: do not use it as a sentence subject when it is withheld. You can use pronouns or a generic reference to the person. State the card facts directly; add no imagined explanations or speculation.
Please describe their job, the city they live in, how they travel to work, their hobby and their pet.

drafts.text: Jonas lives in Prague, a city renowned for its rich history and culture. He uses a car as his primary mode of transportation. His hobby is chess, which he enjoys both competitively and recreationally. Additionally, Jonas has a cat as his pet.

messages.content:
You are the host of a guessing game about a fictional person. The player asks for clues and eventually requests a reveal. Use the secret card as your source of truth. Answer naturally in complete sentences. Do not invent facts.
Use the question as a starting point for a fuller account of the card. Include its answer and extra true facts from categories not requested so far. Volunteer exactly one additional category: the person's name. Do not disclose any other unrequested category. Use the person's name only if requested earlier or now, or if name is the additional category designated above.
Secret card:
City: Prague
Hobby: chess
Pet: cat
Transport: car
Job: gardener
Name: Jonas
Response requirements for this turn: include these categories: job, city, transport, hobby, pet, name. Withhold these categories: none. The name is a category too: do not use it as a sentence subject when it is withheld. You can use pronouns or a generic reference to the person. State the card facts directly; add no imagined explanations or speculation.
Please describe their job, the city they live in, how they travel to work, their hobby and their pet.

drafts.text: Jonas lives in Prague, a city renowned for its rich history and culture. He uses a car as his primary mode of transportation. His hobby is chess, which he enjoys both competitively and recreationally. Jonas is a gardener, dedicating his time to maintaining the city's parks and gardens. His pet is a cat, which he loves to pet and play with.

draft_summary.review_required: Review every candidate pair for truth, relations, and scope; write review.json with drafts_hash, accepted IDs and explicit rejection reasons.

review.note: All generated answers were read. Candidate pairs convey the requested facts and designated extra without an identified wrong relationship. Several use labels/lists rather than conversational sentences; acceptance is task correctness, not naturalness.

pilot_review.reason: No eligible pairs: system trait prompts often produce identical answers or leak the unrequested name.
limitations: A 16-token bin is coarse: accepted answers can still differ substantially in length.
Three instruction variants can generate duplicate answers; pair count is not independent card count.
Prompt location, context length and wording all change between styles; yield differences do not isolate a single cause.

draft_summary.review_required: Review every candidate pair for truth, relations, and scope; write review.json with drafts_hash, accepted IDs and explicit rejection reasons.

review.note: All generated answers were read. Candidate pairs convey the requested facts and designated extra without an identified wrong relationship. Several use labels/lists rather than conversational sentences; acceptance is task correctness, not naturalness.

pilot_review.reason: Compact instructions yield 9 valid candidates from 5 cards, insufficient category and card coverage for the study. Several pairs switch between bare values and labeled lists.
limitations: A 16-token bin is coarse: accepted answers can still differ substantially in length.
Three instruction variants can generate duplicate answers; pair count is not independent card count.
Prompt location, context length and wording all change between styles; yield differences do not isolate a single cause.
